transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora, and I've just completed your post-cataract surgery follow-up check. 

Do you have any questions about your surgery or how you're getting on with your recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I do have a few questions. First, I'm wondering when I can start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a good question! You should avoid any exercise for the first week after surgery, but after that week is up, you can go back to light exercise like gardening.

Just remember to avoid anything strenuous or heavy for about a month after your surgery.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a good question. If you were using eye gel or drops for dry eyes before your operation, it's safe to continue using them unless you've been told otherwise by your doctor.

So you should be fine to carry on with it. If you're not sure about anything specific, it's best to check with your care team.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Some light sensitivity is quite normal as your eyes adjust to the new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, we'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside.

However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to check that further. 

How severe would you say your light sensitivity is?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: It's mostly just a bit of discomfort when I'm outside, so I'll try using sunglasses more often. Thank you for the advice. I have another question: should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It's quite common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after surgery, and it should improve quickly and settle down over time.

How long ago was your surgery? That would help me give you better advice about whether what you're experiencing is normal.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: It was about two weeks ago. So, I guess it's still within the range of normal recovery time, right?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Yes, two weeks is still quite early in your recovery, so some blurriness can still be normal at this stage. It should continue to improve over time.

However, if your vision is getting significantly worse or stays very blurry, we may need to check it to make sure everything's okay. But based on what you've said, you're likely progressing well.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, that's all the questions I had. Thank you for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: That's great! Just to confirm - have all your questions about your cataract surgery recovery been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, you've answered all my questions. Thank you for your assistance!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! Take care, and best of luck with your recovery.
